introduction: On this Sunday, the readings speak of the Sabbath, God's gift of rest. Deuteronomy reminds Israel that the Sabbath recalls their freedom from slavery. In the Gospel, Jesus declares that the Sabbath was made for man, and he heals a man's withered hand. Paul says we carry a treasure in clay vessels. Let us receive the Lord's Day as a gift of freedom and life.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God gives us his day of rest and calls us to do good. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may keep the Lord's Day holy and make it a day of worship, joy and rest. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who are forced to work without rest, and for those exploited in their work: that their dignity may be respected. Let us pray to the Lord.
For the sick and disabled: that Christ may stretch out his hand to heal them and give them hope. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are weary or discouraged: that, though pressed on every side, they may not be crushed. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may set aside time each Sunday for God, for our families and for those in need. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you gave your people the Sabbath as a sign of freedom. Teach us to keep the Lord's Day holy, to rest in you, and to do good to all. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: The Sabbath was made for man
reflection.body:
The commandment to keep the Sabbath is given a reason in Deuteronomy that is easy to miss. It is not only that God rested after creation. It is also about freedom: "You shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out of there." Slaves cannot rest. Free people can. The Sabbath was a weekly reminder that Israel no longer belonged to Pharaoh. And it was for everyone, including servants and strangers, "that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you."

In the Gospel, Jesus is challenged twice about the Sabbath. First, his disciples pick grain as they walk. Jesus answers, "The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath." Then, in the synagogue, a man with a withered hand stands before him while others watch to accuse him. Jesus asks, "Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good or to do harm? To save a life or to kill?" They are silent, and he heals the man: "Stretch out your hand."

For Christians, the Lord's Day is Sunday, the day of the Resurrection. It is still God's gift of freedom: freedom from endless work, freedom to worship, freedom to do good.

Paul reminds us that the life God gives us is fragile: "we have this treasure in clay vessels." "We are pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not to despair." Rest is not a luxury for such vessels; it is part of how God keeps us.

This week, look at how you spend Sunday. Is there time for Mass, for family, for rest and for someone in need? Choose one way to make next Sunday more of a gift to God and to others.
